The page reads as a finished artisan brand: flavours first, then boxes and prices, then the craft, the cook, questions, the order form and the practical details. Every price, pot size, delivery term and dietary statement here is a PLACEHOLDER invented at the owner's request (see _placeholders in site.json) and must be confirmed by Tanu before launch. The four flavour descriptions are Tanu's own words from tanus.uk, lightly punctuated. Section eyebrows are bilingual: {bn, en}, a Bengali word set in Tiro Bangla and its English label. The ordering steps moved from the craft section to the order section, where the sequence is actually used; they are the one place Bengali numerals appear. testimonials is still unused: there are no real reviews, and invented ones are never acceptable.

sections.heading: Baked, not set
sections.lede: Misti doi is usually left to set overnight. Tanu bakes hers, slowly, in the same clay it's served in.
body: Traditional misti doi sets itself. Sweetened milk goes warm into an unglazed clay pot and is left overnight while the culture works. The clay does as much as the milk: it's porous, drawing the whey out through its walls, and that's where the thick texture and faint earthiness of a good one come from.

Tanu keeps the clay and the culture, and adds a slow, low bake. The milk is reduced first until it turns the colour of caramel, then baked in the pot at a gentle heat. The result is denser and silkier than a set doi, with a deeper caramel note. It's inspired by the comfort of mishti doi, in her words, rather than a copy of it.
Every batch is small, made in her kitchen in North Harrow and baked in the week it's delivered.

sections.heading: Good to know
sections.lede: What people ask before their first order. Anything else, just call.

faqs.a: Sweetened set yoghurt, and the dessert Bengal is best known for. Milk is sweetened, poured warm into an unglazed clay pot and left to set, and the clay draws the whey out through its walls as it firms. A good one is thick enough to hold a spoon upright. You'll see it spelled misti doi, mishti doi or mishti dahi; they're all the same thing.

faqs.q: How is baked misti doi different?
faqs.a: Tanu reduces the milk until it caramelises, then bakes it gently in the clay pot instead of leaving it to set. It comes out denser and silkier, with a deeper caramel flavour. If you grew up on the Kolkata sweet-shop version, think of this as a close relative rather than a copy.

faqs.q: Which flavour should I try first?
faqs.a: Mishti Doi, the original. The other three are built on it, so it tells you most about what Tanu does. Buying for someone else? Blush Rose looks the most like a present. For an occasion, choose Saffron Indulgence.

Single pots are £6.50, or £7.50 for Saffron Indulgence. A box of four is £24, six is £34 and twelve is £62. Events of 24 pots or more are £5.50 a pot, or £5.00 from 48. Every price includes the clay pot.

Yes, by hand across London Zones 1–4, Friday to Sunday. Delivery is £6, and free on orders over £50. You can also collect from North Harrow on Saturdays between 10am and 1pm. Further afield? Ask, and we'll see what we can do.

faqs.q: How long does it keep, and will it travel?
faqs.a: Four days in the fridge at 0–5°C. It's happy out of the fridge for up to two hours, so a journey across town is fine. Take it out ten minutes before serving: it's at its best just below room temperature.

Emerald Bliss contains pistachio. The other three don't contain nuts as an ingredient, but everything is made in a kitchen that handles nuts, so no pot can be guaranteed nut-free. Every flavour contains milk.

faqs.q: Is it vegetarian? Is it halal?
faqs.a: It's vegetarian: no gelatine, no egg and no alcohol. It isn't vegan. Tanu's doesn't hold halal certification, but every ingredient is listed in full on the box so you can decide for yourself.

faqs.q: Can you cater a wedding, Eid or Durga Puja?
faqs.a: Yes. We make up to 120 pots a week, with seven days' notice. For big orders we'll send a tasting box first, credited against the final bill, and a 50% deposit holds your date.

faqs.q: What do I do with the pot afterwards?
faqs.a: Keep it. The bhaar is unglazed, food-safe terracotta. Rinse it and use it for a tea light or a small plant, or hand it back on your next delivery and we'll use it again.
